hindi: अब इसके बाद हम शिष्य के उपनयन (दीक्षा) से संबंधित अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the initiation of the pupil.
notes: Standard chapter-opening formula. śiṣyopanayanīya is the chapter title (Śiṣyopanayanīya).

words.gloss: with thin smooth skin and complexion

hindi: गुरु ऐसा कहा गया है: परिश्रमी, तथा बुद्धि, स्मृति और कुशलता से भली-भाँति संपन्न; जिसके मुख, नाक और आँखें सीधी (सुडौल) हों, और जिसकी त्वचा पतली-चिकनी तथा कांति वाली हो।
english: The teacher is said to be diligent and richly endowed with intellect, memory and skill, with straight mouth, nose and eyes, and thin, smooth skin and complexion.
notes: Syntax of the first line is uncertain: 'guruḥ uktaḥ' as printed (the teacher has said) is read as a lead-in to the list of qualities, with the pupil understood as subject; the book's Hindi and English disagree on who is described. Alternative: 'gurūktaḥ' = 'taught by the guru'. Qualities in the verse are those of the pupil. abhiyukta 'diligent' could also be 'attached/engaged'. chavi = lustre/complexion. The unit continues into the next verse (list of qualities). Reading note: guruḥ is the grammatical subject, uktaḥ is passive ('is said to be'); the qualities may therefore describe the teacher, with the pupil introduced only by brahmacārī in the next verse.

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] Hindi says the guru is endowed with intellect etc.; English says "teacher said the student should be..." Sanskrit gurur uktaḥ is ambiguous (likely: the disciple instructed by guru, endowed with buddhi, smṛti, pāṭava) — suggested: Rework translation after confirming reading

words.gloss: having conquered the pairs of opposites

hindi: वह ब्रह्मचारी हो, द्वंद्वों (सुख-दुःख जैसे जोड़ों) को जीत चुका हो, धीर, सदाचारी और स्थिर हो; छह महीने (गुरु के पास) रह चुका हो, समर्थ हो, तथा लज्जा, शुचिता और कला (कुशलता) से युक्त हो।
english: He should be a celibate student (brahmacārin) who has overcome the pairs of opposites, steadfast, of good conduct and firm; one who has lived six months (with the teacher), capable, and endowed with modesty, cleanliness and skill (kalā).
notes: The subject 'he' is understood from the previous verse (the pupil). 'ṣaṇmāsānuṣitaḥ' could be ṣaṇ-māsān uṣitaḥ (having dwelt six months, acc. of duration) or ṣaṭ-māsa-anuṣitaḥ; same sense. 'with whom' he lived is not stated (the teacher is understood by the book). dvaṃdva: the pairs of opposites (the book glosses joy/sorrow). kalā is rendered 'skill'; 'arts' is possible. Correction: brahmacārī is the explicit subject of this unit; it need not be taken over from the previous verse.

words.gloss: of the treatise, its meaning, practice

hindi: शिष्य को तब तक पढ़ाना चाहिए जब तक वह तंत्र, उसके अर्थ और कर्मों के अंत तक न पहुँच जाए। असमय बिजली चमकने और गर्जन होने पर, भूकंप में तथा राहु के दिखाई देने पर (वह अध्ययन न करे)।
english: The pupil is to be taught until he has reached the end of the treatise, its meaning and its practices. And not (to study) when there is untimely lightning and thunder, an earthquake, or the sighting of Rāhu.
notes: Second line begins a prohibition whose verb 'paṭhet' (should recite/study) comes in the next unit; 'na' governs the locatives here and in 2.8. 'gato yāvadantam' read as 'until he has gone to the end'; alternative reading takes gataḥ as describing a pupil who has 'come' to a teacher. tantrārthakarmaṇām: the three items could also be read as one phrase 'the practices of the meaning of the treatise'. Rāhu-darśana is rendered literally; the book glosses it as an eclipse.

words.gloss: with too high or too low (tones)

hindi: पंद्रहवीं तिथि को जब चंद्रमा न हो, अथवा गुरु की अनुपस्थिति में वह पाठ न करे। वह न अविच्छिन्न (बिना टूटे) पदों के साथ, न बहुत धीमे और न बहुत ऊँचे या बहुत नीचे स्वरों में पढ़े।
english: (Nor) should he recite on the fifteenth (lunar day), when the moon is absent, or in the absence of the teacher; and not with unbroken words, not too slowly, and not with tones that are too high or too low.

text_flags.why: possible: na vicchinna-padam (not with broken words); the printed a-vicchinna sits oddly beside the other faults; no reading adopted

notes: Verb 'paṭhet' completes the prohibition begun in the previous unit (na ... paṭhet). pañcadaśī + acandrā: the fifteenth tithi with no moon (taken as new-moon day by the book); the text itself does not say 'new moon'. 'avicchinnapadam' is literally 'with unbroken words', which sits oddly beside the other faults; the intended sense may be 'with words cut off/broken' (na vicchinnapadam); possible textual issue, not changed. 'nīcakaiḥ' is read as the instrumental of a -ka form of nīca/nīcaiḥ.

uncertain.note: [eng] पंचदश्याम् glossed "new moon day" while अचंद्रायाम् is the moonless one; पंचदशी can be full or new moon — suggested: "on the 15th tithi and on a moonless night"

hindi: वह अपने हितैषियों में से एक आचार्य की राजा के समान सेवा करे। आचार्य के सो जाने पर ही वह सोए और उनसे पहले उठे।
english: He should wait upon the teacher, one of his well-wishers, as upon a king. He should lie down only when the teacher has fallen asleep, and rise before him.
notes: 'hitānyatamam' is uncertain: read hita-anyatamam 'one among the well-wishers' (the book's split 'hitān yatamam' is not a valid word division); the sense could be 'the foremost/chosen one among well-wishers'. 'supta eva' is read as supte eva (sandhi e+e/a: supte + eva -> supta eva) giving a locative absolute 'asmin supte' (him being asleep); the book split has suptaḥ, which gives the same sense. 'rājavat' = like a king (treating him with a king's honour).

uncertain.note: [split/src] "हितान् यतमम्" is not a valid split; हितान्यतममाचार्यं unclear — suggested: हित अन्यतमम् आचार्यम् ("the foremost among well-wishers, the teacher")

hindi: वह (गुरु का) केवल नाम न ले, और भले ढंग से भी हँसी-विनोद न करे। वह अटूट (निष्ठावान), अनुद्धत, कठोरता से रहित, सत्य और प्रिय बोलने वाला तथा देखने में प्रिय हो।
english: He should not utter (the teacher's) bare name, nor make sport even in a seemly way. He should be unshakable, not arrogant, not stiff (reading astabdhaḥ), truthful and pleasant in speech, and pleasant to look at.

text_flags.why: Likely: stabdha 'stiff, haughty' contradicts anuddhataḥ and the list of virtues; avagraha apparently lost: anuddhato 'stabdhaḥ = anuddhataḥ astabdhaḥ.

notes: Line 1: the object of 'vinodayet' is not stated; 'na sādhv api' could also be 'nor (does) a good person (amuse)' or 'not even properly'; the book takes it as the teacher being made fun of, which is followed loosely. Subject is the pupil. 'abhedyaḥ' = not to be broken/swayed (steadfast/loyal). Line 2 is translated with the suggested 'astabdhaḥ'; if 'stabdhaḥ' is kept the sense would be 'stiff', which does not fit.
lines_deva: न ब्रूयात्केवलं नाम न साध्वपि विनोदयेत् ॥
lines_iast: na brūyātkevalaṃ nāma na sādhvapi vinodayet ||

uncertain.note: [hindi/eng] Hindi (revere good people / not mock them) and English (not mock him, the teacher) disagree on object; साधु अपि may be adverbial — suggested: "nor amuse himself (with the teacher) even in a good way"
[src] स्तब्धः (arrogant/stiff) contradicts the list of virtues; likely अस्तब्धः (अनुद्धतोऽस्तब्धः); English "gentle" and Hindi "अडिग" follow the wrong reading — suggested: अभेद्योऽनुद्धतोऽस्तब्धः

words.gloss: knowing the meaning of the treatises

hindi: जो बहुश्रुत हो, समय को जानने वाला हो, ग्रंथों का जानकार हो और शास्त्रों के अर्थ को जानता हो, और जो असहाय तथा रोगियों की पुत्र के समान सेवा-उपचार करे।
english: (He should be) much learned, aware of the right time, familiar with the texts, knowing the meaning of the treatises; and one who tends the helpless and the sick as he would a son.
notes: Qualities continue the list of the physician-pupil. 'arthaśāstravit': alternatively 'knowing the Arthaśāstra (science of material welfare/polity)'; the book's 'meaning of treatises' is followed. 'kālavedī' may mean knowing the time for treatment or the seasons; kept literal.

hindi: वह गुरु से अनुमति पाकर 'भिषक्' (वैद्य) शब्द को प्राप्त करता है। परंतु जो केवल शास्त्र को जानता है और कर्मों (व्यावहारिक कार्यों) में निपुण नहीं है, ...
english: Authorised by the teacher, he obtains the name of 'physician' (bhiṣak). But he who knows only the treatise and is not well established in practical work ...
notes: The sentence continues into the next unit ('sa muhyati ...'). 'bhiṣakśabdam' = the designation 'bhiṣak'. 'karman' = practical work/procedures.

hindi: वह रोगी के पास पहुँचते-पहुँचते (हर बार) घबरा जाता है, जैसे डरपोक मनुष्य युद्ध में पहुँचकर घबराता है। और जो शास्त्र से रहित होकर ढिठाई से कर्म करता है, ...
english: Each time he reaches a patient he becomes bewildered, like a timid man on reaching a battle. And he who, devoid of the treatise, acts out of boldness (audacity) ...
notes: The sentence is continued in the next unit ('sa satsu garhām āpnoti ...'). 'prāpya prāpya' is a repetition meaning 'every time he reaches'. dhārṣṭya = boldness/audacity (rashness).

hindi: वह सज्जनों के बीच निंदा पाता है और राजा की ओर से वध (मृत्युदंड) को प्राप्त होता है। (जिसे) रोगों के हेतु, लक्षण, शमन तथा पुनः न होने के विषय में (...)
english: He incurs blame among good people and meets with death (punishment) from the king. (He who has knowledge) of the cause, the sign, the alleviation and the non-recurrence of diseases ...

text_flags.why: Possible: 'caicchaṃti' is plural and 'ca+icch-' would give 'cecch-', not 'caicch-'; subject is singular 'saḥ'. Reading 'vadhaṃ ca ṛcchati' (carcchati) fits the sense; 'vadhaṃ cārhati' (deserves punishment) is another candidate.

notes: Line 1 is the conclusion of the previous sentence (the physician who acts without treatise). The word 'caicchaṃti' is doubtful; the translation follows 'ca ṛcchati' (meets with); alternative 'cārhati' would be 'deserves execution/punishment'. 'vadha' = killing/capital punishment or blows. Line 2 begins a new sentence completed in the next unit (jñānaṃ caturvidhaṃ yasya ...): 'in the cause, sign, alleviation and non-recurrence of diseases'.
lines_deva: स सत्सु गर्हामाप्नोति वधं चैच्छंति राजतः ॥
lines_iast: sa satsu garhāmāpnoti vadhaṃ caicchaṃti rājataḥ ||

uncertain.note: [src/split] "चैच्छंति" is plural and "चै" is not valid sandhi (च+इच्छति = चेच्छति); subject is singular — suggested: वधं चेच्छति / वधं चार्छति राजतः

words.gloss: for the arising of merit and fault

hindi: जिसका ज्ञान चार प्रकार का है (हेतु, लक्षण, शमन, अपुनर्भव के विषय में), वह श्रेष्ठ वैद्य राजा के योग्य है। शस्त्र, शास्त्र और जल गुण तथा दोष की प्रवृत्ति (उत्पत्ति) के लिए होते हैं ...
english: He whose knowledge is fourfold is the best of physicians, worthy of a king. A weapon, treatises and water lead to the arising of merit and of fault ...
notes: Line 1 completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (the fourfold knowledge = cause, sign, alleviation, non-recurrence). Line 2 continues into the next unit (pātrāśrayīṇi ataḥ: they depend on the vessel/user). 'guṇadoṣapravṛttaye' = for the occurrence of good and bad results.
lines_deva: ज्ञानं चतुर्विधं यस्य स राजार्हो भिषक्तमः ॥
lines_iast: jñānaṃ caturvidhaṃ yasya sa rājārho bhiṣaktamaḥ ||

hindi: (ये) पात्र पर आश्रित हैं; अतः (मनुष्य) बहुश्रुतता (विस्तृत अध्ययन) से अपनी प्रज्ञा को बढ़ाए। शास्त्र दीपक के समान है और विशाल बुद्धि दृष्टि है।
english: These depend on the vessel (the user); therefore one should strengthen one's intellect through wide learning. The treatise is indeed like a lamp, and a wide intellect is the sight.

text_flags.why: Possible: 'śrakṣī' is not a word; pātra-āśrayīṇi 'depending on the vessel' fits the preceding line (weapon, treatises, water depend on the user).

notes: First word is garbled; the suggested reading is conjectural (the book's split 'pātra āśraya kṣīṇi' is not a valid word). 'bāhuśrutya' (from bahuśruta) = wide learning. The two metaphors: treatise = lamp, wide intellect = eye/sight.
lines_deva: प्रदीपभूतं शास्त्रं हि दर्शनं विपुला मतिः ॥
lines_iast: pradīpabhūtaṃ śāstraṃ hi darśanaṃ vipulā matiḥ ||

uncertain.note: [src/split] पात्राश्रक्षीण्यतः garbled; split "पात्र आश्रय क्षीणि" non-word — suggested: पात्रापेक्षीण्यतः or पात्राश्रयीण्यतः

hindi: इसलिए इन दोनों (शास्त्र और बुद्धि) का भली-भाँति प्रयोग करके चिकित्सा करता हुआ वह अपराध (भूल) नहीं करता। जो बुलाए जाने पर ही जाता है, सुंदर वेश वाला होकर और शुभ शकुनों को देखकर, ...
english: Therefore, treating with these two well applied, he does not err. He who goes only when called, well dressed, and on good omens, ...
notes: 'tābhyām' refers to the two just named (treatise and intellect, lamp and sight). Line 2 starts a relative clause ('yaḥ ... yāti') completed over the next units and finishing with 'sa vaidyaḥ siddhim aśnute' (2.33). 'sunimittataḥ' = with/after good omens (literal sense; the book glosses auspicious signs).

words.gloss: by the particulars beginning with the cause

hindi: और वहाँ जाकर वह रोगी के प्रयोजन के अतिरिक्त कहीं और अपना मन नहीं लगाता। वह निदान आदि विशेष बातों के द्वारा रोगों की भली-भाँति परीक्षा करता है।
english: And having gone, he sets his mind nowhere other than on the patient's concern. He examines the diseases properly, through the particulars beginning with the cause (nidāna).

text_flags.why: 'kacit' is not a Sanskrit word; kvacit 'anywhere' is intended (va dropped).

notes: The double apostrophe in 'gatvā ''turārthāt' is the printed avagraha-like mark for the elided initial ā of 'ātura'. Continues the relative clause begun in 2.26-27 (yaḥ yāti ...). 'nidānādi' = nidāna (cause) and the other items that follow in the standard list; the text itself only says 'beginning with nidāna'. 'ātura-artha' = the patient's concern/need.
lines_deva: गत्वा ऽऽतुरार्थादन्यत्र न निधत्ते मनः कचित् ॥

words.gram: pres. part. caus. √hā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: और उस (रोगी) के गोपनीय समाचार को वह बाहर प्रकट नहीं करता। और उस (रोगी) के भी चिकित्सा-काल को वह अचानक (बिना विचारे) नहीं निकल जाने देता।
english: And he does not make known outside the report about him that is to be kept secret. Nor, rashly, does he let the time of treatment of him also slip by.
notes: Continues the relative clause (yaḥ yāti ...). 'tad' = that patient. Line 2 is hard: 'sahasā na ca tasyāpi' is read as 'and not abruptly, even of him'; the object is 'kriyākālam ahāpayan' (not letting the treatment time pass). 'tasyā'pi' could also be 'tasyāḥ api' (of it, i.e. the treatment); the book's rendering is followed loosely. 'gopanīyām' agrees with 'vārttām' (secret news).
lines_deva: गोपनीयां च तद्वार्त्तां न प्रकाशयते बहिः ॥
lines_iast: gopanīyāṃ ca tadvārttāṃ na prakāśayate bahiḥ ||

hindi: और जो उपचार करना जानता है, वह वैद्य सिद्धि (सफलता) प्राप्त करता है। वह स्त्रियों से, उनके स्वामी (संरक्षक) के विमुख (अनुपस्थित) होने पर, कोई भेंट (आमिष) न ले।
english: And that physician who knows how to treat attains success. He should not take a gift (āmiṣa) from women when their master (guardian) is turned away.
notes: Line 1 completes the long relative sentence started at 2.26 (yaḥ ... sa vaidyaḥ siddhim aśnute). Line 2 begins a new rule. 'āmiṣa' literally flesh/lure; here 'something desirable, a gift'. 'tadadhyakṣe parāṅmukhe' read as locative absolute 'their lord being turned away' (absent or unwilling); the book's 'absent/away' is one possibility.

hindi: वह स्त्रियों के साथ एकांत में रहना और हँसी-मज़ाक करना छोड़ दे। और उस रोगी को भी, जिससे राजा तथा सज्जन वैद्य द्वेष रखते हों, जो उनसे द्वेष रखता हो, या जो शत्रु हो, ...
english: He should avoid staying with women in private, and joking with them. And (he should avoid) a patient who is hated by the king and by good physicians, who hates them, or who is hostile ...

text_flags.why: Possible: 'tad-veṣin' is not a word; tad-dveṣin 'hating them' fits the sense (dveṣin, with the d of dv- lost).

notes: 'varjayet' of line 1 also governs the accusatives of line 2 and 2.36-37 (the list of patients to be avoided). 'dviṣam' (enemy) is ambiguous: enemy of the physician, or of the king; the book takes 'enemy'. 'nṛpasadvaidyaiḥ' = by the king and good physicians (dvandva).
lines_deva: नारीभिश्च रहसि स्थानं परिहासं च वर्जयेत् ॥
lines_iast: nārībhiśca rahasi sthānaṃ parihāsaṃ ca varjayet ||

hindi: (और ऐसे रोगी को भी छोड़ दे) जो उग्र हो, शोक से पीड़ित हो, डरपोक हो, कृतघ्न हो, अपने को वैद्य मानने वाला हो; जिसके पास साधनों का अभाव हो, जो व्याकुल हो, आज्ञा न मानने वाला हो, अथवा जिसकी आयु बीत चुकी हो।
english: (He should avoid a patient) who is fierce, stricken with grief, timid, ungrateful, one who thinks himself a physician; who lacks equipment (means), is agitated, disobedient, or whose life-span is spent.
notes: Accusatives continue from 'varjayet' (2.35): the list of patients to be avoided. 'vaidyamānin' = one who fancies himself a physician (a patient conceited about medical knowledge). 'hīnopakaraṇa' = lacking the means (attendants, materials); not specified in the text. 'gatāyuṣam' literally 'one whose lifespan has gone'.

hindi: जीने की इच्छा रखने वाला रोगी भी, पहले बताए गुणों से रहित और चिकित्सा को बेचने वाले वैद्यों को छोड़ दे; क्योंकि वे निश्चय ही मृत्यु के आगे-आगे चलने वाले हैं।
english: Even a sick person who wishes to live should avoid physicians who lack the qualities described earlier and who sell treatment, for they are indeed the forerunners of death.
notes: The governing verb (something like 'should avoid', parivarjayet) is not in the unit; it is understood from the preceding verse. 'vaidyān' in line 2 is the object of that verb and is qualified by 'varjitān' and 'kriyā-vikrayiṇaḥ'. Literally kriyā-vikrayin = 'one who sells the (medical) act/treatment'.

hindi: वैद्य, द्रव्य, परिचारक और रोगी, ये चिकित्सा के चार पाद बताए गए हैं; इनमें से प्रत्येक चार गुणों वाला है।
english: The physician, the medicines, the attendant and the patient are declared to be the four quarters (pāda) of treatment; each one of them has four qualities.
notes: 'taccaturguṇaṃ' read as tat + catuḥ-guṇam, 'each of them is fourfold in qualities'. pāda = quarter/foot, the four supports of treatment.

words.gloss: one who has taken the meaning of the treatises
one who has seen the work done

hindi: वैद्य कुशल हो, गुरु से शास्त्रों का अर्थ ग्रहण किए हुए हो, कर्म को देखा हुआ हो और पवित्र हो। औषध अनेक प्रकार के कल्पों वाला, अनेक गुणों वाला, सम्पन्न और उपयुक्त हो।
english: The physician should be skilled, one who has received the meaning of the treatises from a teacher, who has seen the work done, and who is pure. The medicine should have many preparations and many qualities, be well endowed, and be suitable.
notes: tīrtha is literally a ford, here understood as a teacher or authoritative source. 'sampanna' = fully endowed/perfect. 'kalpa' = preparation (form in which a drug is made up). The verb 'is' is understood.

words.gloss: one who can make known (his condition)

hindi: परिचारक अनुरक्त, पवित्र, कुशल और बुद्धिमान हो। रोगी धनवान, वैद्य के वश में रहने वाला, अपनी बात बता सकने वाला और मनोबल से युक्त भी हो।
english: The attendant should be devoted, pure, skilled and intelligent. The patient should be wealthy, obedient to the physician, able to make his condition known, and also possessed of mental strength (sattva).
notes: jñāpaka is taken as 'one who informs (the physician of his complaint)'; alternative: 'one who understands/is informed'. 'sattva' = strength of mind.

hindi: क्योंकि वैद्य के गुणहीन होने पर बाकी पाद गुणवान होते हुए भी निरर्थक हो जाते हैं, और क्योंकि गुणवान वैद्य अन्य पादों से रहित रोगियों को भी (जीवित) चला लेता है।
english: Since, when the physician lacks qualities, the other quarters are useless even though they have qualities, and since a qualified physician can keep going even patients who lack the other quarters,
notes: Both lines are 'yat' clauses (since ...), completed by the next verse ('therefore they know him as the chief cause'). 'sapādahīnān' is read as saḥ (sa before a consonant, as often in verse) + pāda-hīnān; the book split agrees. 'pāda-hīna' = lacking quarters (the other three), taken as 'lacking some of the other quarters'. 'yāpayet' = sustain, keep going (palliate). 'ārttān' is the printed spelling of ārtān. Alternative: sapāda-hīnān could be read as one compound ('lacking a quarter'); the reading with saḥ is kept because the book split agrees.

hindi: इसलिए चिकित्सा का प्रधान कारण उसी (वैद्य) को वे जानते हैं। रोग दो प्रकार का है, साध्य और असाध्य; और वे दोनों फिर दो-दो प्रकार के हैं।
english: Therefore they know him (the physician) alone as the chief cause of treatment. Disease is twofold, curable and incurable; and these two are again each twofold.

text_flags.why: Possible scan error: 'asādhyaiti' is not a sandhi form; sādhyaḥ asādhyaḥ iti gives sādhyo'sādhya iti, and the line then has 16 syllables (printed form has 15).

notes: 'tam' (him) refers to the physician of the previous verse. 'dvidhā' in 'tau tu punar dvidhā' = each of the two is again twofold (the four named in the next verse).

words.gloss: of one with a self-controlled mind

hindi: ये चार हैं: सुसाध्य, कृच्छ्रसाध्य, याप्य और जो उपक्रम-रहित है। (सुसाध्य रोग होता है) ऐसे शरीर में जो सब औषधियों को सहन कर सके, युवा पुरुष में, जिसने अपने आप को जीत रखा हो।
english: They are: easily curable, curable with difficulty, to be sustained (palliable), and the one that admits no remedy. [Easily curable is the disease] in a body able to bear all medicines, of a young man who has mastered himself,
notes: The sentence continues into the next unit (unit 27): the conditions of the easily curable disease. The main clause is therefore not in this unit; the bracketed words in the English are understood, not stated here. 'jitātman' = self-controlled (alternatively 'with a conquered mind').

words.gloss: with slight cause, slight early signs and slight signs
whose dūṣya, place, season and constitution are unlike (the disease)
when the quarters are well endowed

hindi: (सुसाध्य वह रोग है) जो मर्मों में न जाने वाला हो, जिसके हेतु, पूर्वरूप और रूप थोड़े हों, जिसमें उपद्रव न हों; जिसके दूष्य, देश, ऋतु और प्रकृति (रोग के) समान न हों, और पादों की सम्पन्नता हो।
english: [The easily curable disease is one] that does not reach the vital spots, has a slight cause, slight early signs and slight signs, and no complications; in which the dūṣya (affected substance), place, season and constitution are not alike (to the disease), and when the quarters are well endowed.
notes: Continuation of the previous unit. 'agra-rūpa' is read as 'early (premonitory) sign' and 'rūpa' as the sign proper; alternative: agra-rūpa-rūpa as a single member. 'atulya' is taken to mean 'unlike (the disease)': the text states only 'atulya', the object of comparison is understood. 'dūṣya' = that which is vitiated (gloss only; no modern equivalent given). The English and Hindi bracketed supply of the subject is from context.

words.gloss: with a single doṣa and path

hindi: ग्रह अनुकूल हों, एक ही दोष और एक ही मार्ग वाला, नया और सरल रोग सुखसाध्य होता है; उसके उपाय सरल होते हैं और वह थोड़े समय में ठीक हो जाता है।
english: With the planets favourable, a disease with a single doṣa and a single path, new, and easy is easily curable; its means are easy, and it is cured in a short time.
notes: graha is taken as 'planet'; it can also mean a seizing influence. 'mārga' = path/channel (of the doṣa). The subject 'disease' is understood. 'sukha' in line 1 is taken as 'easy (to deal with)'.

words.gloss: having surgery and the like as the means

hindi: कृच्छ्रसाध्य रोग कठिन और बड़े उपायों से और देर से (सिद्ध होता है); वह असाध्य के लक्षणों से मिला हुआ होता है, और उसके साधन शस्त्र आदि होते हैं।
english: The one curable with difficulty (is cured) by difficult and great means and after a long time; it is mixed with signs of incurability, and its means are surgery and the like.
notes: The verb 'is cured' is understood from the previous verse. Line 2 follows the grammar as printed and so still describes the kṛcchra-sādhya disease; the book's English and Hindi attach line 2 differently (as describing the incurable), which the Sanskrit does not support. 'mahadbhiḥ' modifies upāyaiḥ.

hindi: आयु के शेष रहने के कारण याप्य रोग हितकर उपायों से चलता रहता है; इसके विपरीत होने पर प्रायः वह थोड़ा सुख देकर थोड़े से कारण से फैल जाता है।
english: Because life remains, the disease to be sustained (yāpya) is kept going by wholesome measures; in the contrary case, for the most part, after giving slight comfort it spreads on account of a slight cause.
notes: 'prāyaḥ viparyaye' is placed between the two clauses; it can attach to either (mostly, when things are contrary / when wholesome measures are lacking). The text does not say what the contrary is; read as the lack of wholesome measures. 'saḥ' = the yāpya disease.
lines_deva: दत्त्वा ऽल्पं सुखमल्पेन हेतुना स प्रतन्यते ॥

words.gloss: to the state of having no remainder

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. pra-√pat

hindi: कर्म से उत्पन्न रोग, निश्चित आयु वाले में, पूरी तरह शेष-रहित अवस्था को नहीं पहुँचता, अर्थात् पूर्ण रूप से नहीं मिटता। यहाँ रोगी, गिरते हुए के समान, हितकर उपायों रूपी टेकों से थामा जाता है।
english: The disease born of past action, in one whose lifespan is fixed, does not reach the state of leaving no remainder. Here the patient, like one who is falling, is held up by wholesome things as by props.
notes: 'aśeṣatā' literally 'state of being without remainder', understood as complete removal. 'viṣkambha' = prop, bolt; the simile is a falling (house or person) held by props: the text says only 'prapatan iva', so the thing falling is the patient.

hindi: दूसरा, असाध्य रोग सब चिकित्साओं को लाँघ जाता है और उसे अस्वीकार करना चाहिए। इसलिए वह, अत्यन्त विपरीत अवस्था में स्थित होने के कारण, उपेक्षा के ही योग्य है।
english: The other, the incurable, goes beyond all treatments and is to be refused. Therefore that one, standing in extreme reversal, is simply to be disregarded.
notes: The printed 'upekṣyaevāsau' joins upekṣyaḥ eva asau (hiatus after -aḥ is correct, only the space is missing). 'atyanta-viparyaya' is rendered literally as 'extreme reversal/contrariness'; what is reversed (the course of the disease, or the natural state) is not stated. 'kriyāḥ sarvāḥ ... ativartate' = it passes beyond all treatments (they do not work on it).

words.gloss: in whom fatal signs are seen

hindi: (वह असाध्य रोग) भ्रम, मोह और अरति करने वाला, जिसमें मृत्यु-सूचक अरिष्ट लक्षण दिखाई दिए हों और जो इन्द्रियों का नाश करने वाला है। (वैद्य) पहले रोग की इस प्रकार परीक्षा करके तब चिकित्सा आरम्भ करे।
english: [That incurable one is] causing giddiness, delusion and unease, with fatal signs (riṣṭa) seen, and destroying the senses. Having first examined the disease in this way, one should then begin treatment.
notes: GROUPING: line 1 describes the incurable disease of the previous unit (it belongs with the sentence of 2.62-63), while line 2 starts a new sentence ('having examined the disease first, one should begin treatment'); the two lines of this unit are not one sentence. 'akṣa' = sense organ (or eye); rendered 'senses'. 'riṣṭa' = sign of approaching death (technical word). The subject of 'ārabheta' (the physician) is understood.

words.gloss: loss of own interest, knowledge and fame

hindi: अन्यथा (वैद्य) अपने प्रयोजन, विद्या और यश की हानि निश्चित रूप से पाएगा। दुर्बल व्यक्ति में दो साध्य रोगों का भी संयोग असाध्यता को पहुँच जाता है।
english: Otherwise he would surely incur loss of his own interest, his knowledge and his fame. Even the combination of two curable diseases, in a weak person, goes to incurability.
notes: 'sva-artha' = one's own aim or interest (wealth, livelihood); alternative: 'svārtha' as 'own purpose'. The subject of 'āpnuyāt' (the physician who does not examine first) is understood. 'sādhyayoḥ' is dual genitive (of two curable [diseases]); 'abalinaḥ' is read as genitive/ablative of 'abalin' (weak) in the sense 'in a weak person'. GROUPING: line 1 completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (line 2: examine first, then begin treatment; otherwise loss of ...); line 2 starts a new sentence that continues into the next unit.

words.gloss: the meeting of curable and incurable

hindi: इसलिए साध्य और असाध्य के मेल को असाध्य ही जानना चाहिए। असाध्य कभी साध्य नहीं होता, किन्तु साध्य असाध्य हो जाता है।
english: Therefore one should know the meeting of a curable and an incurable (disease) to be incurable only. The incurable does not become curable, but the curable does become incurable.
notes: 'asādhyam' is the predicate of 'samāgamam' (to be known as incurable).
lines_deva: नासाध्यः साध्यतां याति साध्यो याति त्वसाध्यतां ॥
lines_iast: nāsādhyaḥ sādhyatāṃ yāti sādhyo yāti tvasādhyatāṃ ||

hindi: पादों के अपचार से और दैव से रोग दूसरी अवस्था को पहुँच जाते हैं। विषैले सर्प का विष श्रेष्ठ है, अथवा जलती हुई अग्नि, अथवा इसी प्रकार कुछ और; वाक्य अगले श्लोक में पूरा होता है।
english: From mismanagement of the quarters and from fate, diseases pass into another state. Better the venom of a venomous snake, or a blazing fire, or else too [the sentence is completed in the next verse]
notes: GROUPING: line 1 completes the previous sentence, line 2 starts a new one that runs into the next unit: 'better (to swallow) snake venom or blazing fire than to ...' (the verb upayuñjīta is in 2.72). The thing that is 'better' is stated in the next unit. 'avasthāntara' = another state/stage (of the disease). 'āśīviṣa' = a snake whose venom is in its fangs.

words.gloss: should make use of or accept
text unclear: unseen, become, physician, unrighteousness

hindi: ... रोगी से आमिष (लाभ, लालच या मांस) नहीं (लेना?) ... (यह भाग पाठ की गड़बड़ी के कारण अस्पष्ट है) ... इस प्रकार रोगियों में श्रेष्ठ वैद्य।
english: [Better ...] to use ..., but not to take from the sick a gain (āmiṣa), ... [the words 'rūpeṇāñjanāt' are unclear] ... [the words 'parokṣabhūtavaidyādharma' are unclear] ... thus (is) the best physician among the sick.

text_flags.why: Possible corruption: the editors flagged the line as garbled; 'by form, from ointment' gives no sense and the sandhi 'rūpeṇāñjanāt' is doubtful.
Possible corruption: flagged by the editors as garbled; the line has 17 syllables (one too many) and 'dharma iti' would be the expected sandhi form.

notes: Both lines are flagged by the editors as damaged. The sentence continues from the previous unit ('better the venom of a snake or blazing fire ... to use (upayuñjīta), but not ...'); the 'varam ... na tu' structure is probable ('better X than Y') but the exact objects are not recoverable. The book's Hindi (a fraudulent doctor) and English (accepting gains from the patient) disagree and are both speculative; I give only the legible words: 'should use', 'not from the sick', 'āmiṣa' (gain/bait/flesh), 'iti ārtteṣu bhiṣagvaraḥ' (thus, among the sick, the best physician). 'vaidyādharma' could be vaidya-adharma(ḥ) (physician's unrighteousness) or vaidya-dharma(ḥ) with a stray ā. Nothing here should be relied on.

uncertain.note: [src/hindi/eng] Sanskrit garbled (आर्त्तादामिषं रूपेणाञ्जनात्); Hindi (quack) and English (accept gains from patient) disagree — suggested: unknown
[src/hindi/eng] परोक्षभूतवैद्याधर्म garbled; translations speculative — suggested: unknown

hindi: जो (वैद्य इस प्रकार) आचरण करता है, वह सिद्धार्थ (सफल-मनोरथ) होकर सबको पार कर जाता है।
english: But he who conducts himself (in this way), his purposes accomplished, surpasses everything.
notes: 'varttate' (printed double t) = vartate. 'in this way' is understood from the previous unit, whose text is damaged; the manner of conduct is therefore not certain. 'ativarttate' = goes beyond / surpasses (could also mean 'overcomes').

words.gloss: on the initiation of the student

hindi: इस प्रकार शिष्योपनयनीय नामक दूसरा अध्याय ।। २ ।।
english: Thus the second chapter, named Śiṣyopanayanīya (on the initiation of the student). || 2 ||
notes: Closing colophon of chapter 2; the verb 'ends' is understood.
